source.snippet: Currently, MCP servers are configured globally and exposed to every workspace's agent. There's no way to restrict a server to specific workspaces or exclude one from workspaces where it doesn't belong. This request proposes a two-tier model: global MCP servers (current behavior, available everywhere) and workspace-scoped servers (available only in the workspaces that enable them). The global-only model creates two friction points: Security and scope — tools with broad permissions leak into workspaces that should not have access to them.

problem_statement: Teams running multi-workspace LLM platforms (e.g. AnythingLLM) cannot restrict which MCP tool-servers are available per workspace, so sensitive integrations are exposed across all agents with no access control, creating security and compliance risk.
target_segment: DevOps engineers and IT admins at SMBs/mid-market companies deploying self-hosted or cloud LLM platforms with multiple teams or clients.
notes: Buyer context: companies paying for LLM infrastructure/hosting who need compliance-grade workspace isolation. Feature request filed against an open-source product — indicates unmet need that a managed/commercial layer could address. Single GitHub issue but touches a structural gap in the entire MCP ecosystem. Willingness to pay implied by enterprise security requirements.
